question: During otoscopic examination of an adult patient, which direction should the pinna be retracted to straighten the external auditory canal and obtain the best view of the tympanic membrane?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Downward and backward is the direction for infants and young children (under 1 year), where the canal is shorter and more horizontal. Applying this technique to an adult will worsen the canal angle and obscure the view.

Correct. In adults, the pinna is retracted upward and backward to straighten the S-shaped external auditory canal. This opens the canal, aligns the cartilaginous and bony segments, and provides a clear line of sight to the tympanic membrane.
Pulling the pinna directly forward does not correct the angulation of the external auditory canal and will not improve speculum entry or the view of the tympanic membrane.

Upward and forward is not the standard technique for adults. The backward component is essential to correct the posterosuperior angulation of the bony canal. Upward and forward would not straighten the canal adequately.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: adults — upward and backward; infants and toddlers — downward and backward. The difference reflects the developmental change in external auditory canal orientation.
Correct. Adults require upward-and-backward pinna traction; infants require downward-and-backward. This directional distinction is commonly tested in practical OSCEs.
